Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 1
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA
Starting / Power Problems — Detailed Troubleshooting
Manual
This manual is organized as seven independent troubleshooting topics. Each topic begins on a new page and
provides a sequential procedure, including small checks that should be completed before moving to the next
step.
Model basis: Samsung's official support page lists the WA5471ABP/XAA User Manual, version 4, modified May 3, 2016. The manual's
troubleshooting section specifically covers the 'Will not start' condition and includes checks for the door, power connection, water faucets,
Start/Pause, Child Lock, and circuit protection. turn0search4I
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 2

1. Washer does not turn on
Problem description: The control panel remains completely dark or pressing the Power button produces no
response.
Procedure

Step 1. Make sure the washer is not currently in a power interruption. Check whether lights or another
appliance on the same electrical circuit are working.

Step 2. Go to the washer's power cord and confirm that the plug is fully inserted into the electrical outlet. Do
not rely only on looking at the plug; make sure it has not become partially disconnected.

Step 3. Inspect the plug and the visible portion of the power cord without touching exposed conductors. Look
for cuts, melted areas, discoloration, loose parts, or signs of overheating.

Step 4. If the cord and plug appear normal, press the Power button once. Wait a few seconds and observe the
control panel for any lights or display activity.

Step 5. If there is still no response, check the electrical outlet using a safe method. If you are not comfortable
testing an outlet, have a qualified person verify that the outlet is supplying power.

Step 6. If the outlet has no power, do not attempt to repair the household wiring yourself. Restore the
household electrical supply or contact a qualified electrician.

Step 7. If the outlet has power, disconnect the washer from the outlet before doing any further external
inspection. Wait briefly, reconnect it securely, and press Power again.

Step 8. If the washer remains completely unresponsive even though the outlet has power, stop the procedure.
The problem may be inside the washer's power/control system and should be diagnosed by service
personnel.
After completing the steps
Do not remove the washer's electrical covers or attempt to test live internal components as a DIY repair.

Safety: Do not bypass a fuse, circuit breaker, grounding connection, or other protective device.
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 3

2. Washer does not start
Problem description: The control panel powers on, but the washer does not begin the selected wash cycle.
Procedure

Step 1. Press Power and confirm that the control panel turns on normally.

Step 2. Make sure the washer door/lid is fully closed. Open it and close it again firmly so the machine can
detect the closed position.

Step 3. Check both water-source faucets. Make sure they are open so the washer can obtain the water
required to begin the cycle.

Step 4. Check that the water inlet hoses are connected and are not obviously kinked or crushed.

Step 5. Select the required wash cycle and any desired options.

Step 6. Press the Start/Pause button deliberately once. Do not assume that selecting a cycle alone starts the
washer.

Step 7. After pressing Start/Pause, wait briefly. The washer may make clicking sounds before filling because it
checks the door lock and performs a quick drain. This is described in the model's troubleshooting guidance
and is not by itself evidence of a failure. 

Step 8. If the washer still does not start, check whether Child Lock is active. If the Child Lock indicator is
present, follow the Child Lock procedure in Topic 5.

Step 9. If the display shows an information/error code, record the exact code before attempting additional
troubleshooting.

Step 10. If all external checks are normal and the washer still refuses to start, stop the procedure and arrange
service rather than opening the machine.
After completing the steps
Samsung's model-specific troubleshooting lists the closed door, plugged-in washer, open water faucets,
Start/Pause, Child Lock, and fuse/circuit-breaker checks for a washer that will not start.

Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 4

3. Start/Pause button not responding
Problem description: The washer has power, but pressing Start/Pause does not start or resume the
operation.
Procedure

Step 1. Look at the control panel and confirm that the washer is powered on.

Step 2. Check the Child Lock indicator. If Child Lock is active, the other buttons are locked and pressing them
may cause the Child Lock indicator to blink.

Step 3. If Child Lock is active, press and hold the Spin and Soil Level buttons simultaneously for
approximately 3 seconds.

Step 4. Wait for the Child Lock indicator to turn off. Then press Start/Pause once and observe whether the
washer responds.

Step 5. If Child Lock was not active, make sure the control panel is dry and clean. Do not press buttons with
wet hands or while liquid is present on the panel.

Step 6. Confirm that you have selected a valid wash cycle before pressing Start/Pause.

Step 7. Press Start/Pause once and wait. Avoid repeatedly pressing the button because repeated inputs can
make it harder to determine whether the washer has accepted the command.

Step 8. If the washer still does not respond to Start/Pause, check whether another information/error code is
displayed.

Step 9. If the Power button works but Start/Pause consistently does not respond after these checks, the
control interface or another control component may require service diagnosis.
After completing the steps
On this model, Child Lock specifically prevents the other buttons from operating while Power remains
available. The manual specifies Spin + Soil Level held for about 3 seconds to activate/deactivate it.

Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 5

4. Washer stops immediately after starting
Problem description: The washer appears to accept the start command but stops almost immediately or
does not proceed into normal washing.
Procedure

Step 1. Observe the display immediately after the washer stops. If an information/error code appears, write it
down exactly.

Step 2. Open and close the door/lid firmly. Make sure no clothing or other object is preventing it from closing
correctly.

Step 3. Press Start/Pause again and observe whether the washer begins operation.

Step 4. Check that both water-source faucets are open.

Step 5. Look at the inlet hoses and make sure they are connected and not sharply kinked or crushed.

Step 6. Check whether Child Lock is active. If it is, deactivate it using the procedure in Topic 5.

Step 7. Listen to the washer during the first moments after starting. Clicking sounds before filling can be part
of the normal start sequence because the washer checks the door lock and performs a quick drain.


Step 8. If the washer repeatedly stops at the same point, do not continue restarting it over and over. Record
the exact sequence of events and any displayed code.

Step 9. If the washer stops with no obvious external cause, service diagnosis may be required.
After completing the steps
Repeated immediate stopping should not be treated as a normal operating condition if the basic door, water,
controls, and information-code checks do not resolve it.
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 6

5. Child Lock preventing operation
Problem description: The washer appears powered, but buttons other than Power do not respond. The Child
Lock indicator may illuminate or blink.
Procedure

Step 1. Look at the control panel and identify whether the Child Lock indicator is illuminated.

Step 2. Press a button other than Power once. If the buttons are locked, the Child Lock indicator may blink
instead of allowing the command.

Step 3. To deactivate Child Lock, press and hold the Spin and Soil Level buttons simultaneously.

Step 4. Continue holding both buttons for approximately 3 seconds.

Step 5. Release both buttons and check the control panel. The Child Lock indicator should no longer indicate
that the controls are locked.

Step 6. Press Start/Pause once to check whether normal operation has returned.

Step 7. If the Child Lock function was intentionally enabled for safety, do not deactivate it until you are ready to
operate the washer.

Step 8. Remember that the Child Lock setting can remain active even after the washer is powered off and
back on. 

Step 9. If the controls remain locked even after the specified button combination is performed correctly, record
the behavior and arrange service.
After completing the steps
The model manual states that Child Lock locks the buttons except Power, and that Spin + Soil Level held
simultaneously for approximately 3 seconds controls the function. 
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 7

6. Circuit breaker / fuse trips
Problem description: The electrical circuit supplying the washer trips a breaker or a fuse opens when the
washer is used.
Procedure

Step 1. Stop using the washer immediately if the breaker trips or the fuse opens.

Step 2. Do not repeatedly reset the breaker or replace the fuse while the washer remains connected if the
protective device continues to trip.

Step 3. Disconnect the washer from the electrical outlet if this can be done safely and there is no sign of
burning, arcing, or physical damage.

Step 4. Look only at the accessible plug, cord, and outlet. Check for visible melting, discoloration, smoke
residue, or a burning smell.

Step 5. If there is visible damage, smoke, burning odor, sparking, or heat around the plug/outlet, do not
reconnect the washer.

Step 6. If there is no visible damage and the household circuit is otherwise normal, have the circuit and outlet
checked by a qualified electrician before returning the washer to service.

Step 7. Do not substitute a fuse with one of a different rating and do not bypass the circuit breaker.

Step 8. If a qualified person confirms the outlet/circuit is suitable but the washer continues to trip the protection
device, the washer requires service diagnosis.

Step 9. Do not open the control panel or attempt internal electrical measurements unless you are a qualified
service professional using the appropriate service procedure.
After completing the steps
Samsung's user troubleshooting guidance includes checking the fuse or resetting the circuit breaker for a
washer that will not start; repeated trips should be treated as an electrical fault rather than repeatedly reset.


Safety: Electrical protection devices exist to prevent hazardous conditions. Never bypass or defeat them.
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Starting / Power Problems
Page 8

7. Washer turns off unexpectedly
Problem description: The washer loses power or the control panel becomes inactive during a cycle without
the user intentionally turning it off.
Procedure

Step 1. Note exactly when the washer turns off: during filling, washing, draining, spinning, or another part of
the cycle.

Step 2. Check whether other electrical devices in the same area also lost power. If they did, the issue may be
with the household electrical supply.

Step 3. Check the household circuit breaker only if it can be done safely. If it has tripped, do not repeatedly
reset it if it trips again.

Step 4. If household power is available, inspect the washer's accessible plug and cord for obvious damage
without touching damaged areas.

Step 5. If power returns to the washer, observe the control panel and check whether an information/error code
is displayed.

Step 6. Record the exact code, if any, before switching the washer off again.

Step 7. Try to determine whether the shutdown happens at the same point in the same cycle. A repeatable
shutdown is useful information for service diagnosis.

Step 8. If the washer operates normally after a household power interruption, monitor it for recurrence rather
than repeatedly restarting an unstable machine.

Step 9. If the washer repeatedly shuts down while the household electrical supply remains stable, stop using it
and arrange service diagnosis.

Step 10. If there is a burning smell, smoke, visible electrical damage, abnormal heat, or repeated breaker
operation, disconnect the washer if safe and do not use it again until it has been inspected.
After completing the steps
Unexpected shutdowns can have causes outside the washer, such as a household power interruption, so
identifying whether other devices also lost power is an important first check.
